inputs.root_cause: Events 216/217 established a repeatable pattern for the UBL schema-conformance cluster; this tick applies it to model/lines.py's CreditNoteLine/Response/DocumentReference types, the cluster's next already-modeled component family.
inputs.obligation_targeted: The same 6-obligation cluster narrowed by events 216/217 (SAL-UBL-OBL-03AF3A7D3A76F362 and its cross-capability duplicates) -- extended with additional coverage, still not closed
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 8 new tests prove validate() now also detects cardinality violations for cac:CreditNoteLine's ID/CreditedQuantity fields, cac:Response's ResponseCode field, and cac:DocumentReference's DocumentTypeCode field, while correctly never flagging Response.Description (genuinely minOccurs=0 maxOccurs=UNBOUNDED per the schema, unlike its sibling field ResponseCode), proven as its own dedicated test.
inputs.regression_tier: full ubl package suite (tests/python/ubl) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Surveyed model/lines.py's other already-modeled dataclasses beyond OrderLine/DespatchLine (whose own fields are mostly required nested aggregates, not many direct optional leaf fields worth checking): CreditNoteLine (id/credited_quantity/line_extension_amount/item), Response (response_code/description), DocumentReference (id/document_type_code).

2. Extracted CreditNoteLineType's, ResponseType's, and DocumentReferenceType's complete field lists with exact minOccurs/maxOccurs directly from the pinned OASIS UBL 2.3 release ZIP (same source as events 216/217). Found a second genuine schema/model discrepancy, honestly documented rather than silently resolved: ResponseType declares cbc:Description as minOccurs=0 maxOccurs=UNBOUNDED (repeatable), even though this package's own Response.description field models only a single value -- deliberately excluded from the new check, the same discipline already applied to PaymentMeans.PaymentID in the prior slice.

3. Added 3 new QNAME constants, 3 new frozensets, and 3 new entries to the existing qname-keyed _CARDINALITY_CHECKED_COMPONENTS dispatch dict (introduced in event 217's refactor specifically to make this kind of extension mechanical).

4. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: a single CreditNoteLine ID validates cleanly; two IDs are flagged; a Response with two ResponseCode values is flagged; a Response with multiple Description values is correctly NOT flagged; a DocumentReference with two DocumentTypeCode values is flagged -- all 5 cases correct on the first attempt.
5. Ran the full pre-existing ubl suite (904 tests, zero new fixtures) against the extended check to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 904 passed unchanged.

6. Wrote 8 formal tests. One self-correction during writing: the first draft's cac:Response fixtures were incorrectly wrapped in a <cac:DiscrepancyResponse> element (confusing a sibling XSD field name from CreditNoteLineType's own field list with the actual cac:Response element structure) -- caught immediately by 1 test failure (report unexpectedly valid), fixed by using <cac:Response> directly (confirmed via response_of()'s actual caller, document_response_of, which calls find(node, 'Response')), after which all 8 tests passed.

7. Ran ruff (clean), the full ubl suite (912 passed, was 904, +8), and the full 6-format regression (3278 passed, was 3270, +8; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

8. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-d26655bb50bbdf70, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
